Question: What is the effectiveness of mRNA vaccines against COVID-19 variants?

Hypothetical Abstract:

Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of currently authorized mRNA vaccines (BNT162b2 and mRNA-2020/414) against infection and severe disease caused by emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants.
Methods: This retrospective analysis utilized data from a large healthcare system representing diverse demographics. We examined patient records of individuals vaccinated with BNT162b2 and mRNA-2020/414 and subsequently diagnosed with confirmed COVID-19 infection, categorizing infections by circulating variant.
Results: Preliminary findings demonstrate a significant reduction in risk of symptomatic infection across all variants compared to unvaccinated individuals. Specifically, BNT162b2 exhibited approximately 75% effectiveness against the original wild-type strain, 60% against the Delta variant, and 50% against the Omicron variant. mRNA-2020/414 showed similar, albeit slightly lower, efficacy rates. Booster doses of both vaccines provided substantial protection against severe disease, particularly against the Omicron subvariants.
Conclusion: mRNA vaccines maintain a demonstrable level of effectiveness against COVID-19 variants, though waning immunity necessitates ongoing booster vaccination to mitigate risk of severe outcomes, particularly with the emergence of newer subvariants.
